entries.ai_recommendation_summary: Always-On Sandbox was recommended because the team needs immediate, shared, read-only API access with no time to wait for provisioning.
entries.rationale: The scenario requires access without waiting for a reservation. It also requires non-admin, read-only API calls. Cisco defines them (Always-On-Sandbox) as shared, no-reservation environments with admin access.

entries.ai_recommendation_summary: Reservation Sandbox was recommended since the team requires private, administrative access and can accept setup time and VPN connection.
entries.rationale: The team wants administrative control to test changes in a configuration in a private area. They are ready to schedule access and connect through a VPN.

entries.ai_recommendation_summary: DevNet Learning Lab was recommended because the user needs guided, step-by-step instructional content rather than a live execution environment.
entries.rationale: A beginner who needs structured guided instruction, before working independently matches the purpose of Learning Labs. Learning Labs deliver step‑by‑step content instead of hands‑on device access.

entries.ai_recommendation_summary: Cisco Code Exchange was recommended so the developer can browse existing community and Cisco-maintained automation repositories before building a new solution.
entries.rationale: The developer wants to look at the community and Cisco-run repositories to find automation examples. This is the goal of Cisco Code Exchange, which used to be called Automation Exchange.
